title: If Not, If Necessary: Conditions Without Si

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know conditions without *si* from B2 Unit 10: *de* + infinitive (*De ser necesario*, *De no haber existido*) and the gerund (*Estudiando más, aprobarías*). They are shorter and sound more written. The literacy campaign and the Cold War are full of "if" thinking: what would have happened without the campaign, what is done if necessary.

sections.title: Conditions without si
rows: De no haber existido la campaña, muchas personas no habrían aprendido a leer.
*de* + *haber* + participle = *si no hubiera existido*: had the campaign not existed
De ser necesario, los brigadistas se quedaban a dormir en la casa.
De haber sabido leer, los campesinos habrían podido escribir cartas.
*de haber sabido* = *si hubieran sabido*: had they known how to read
Estudiando cada noche, aprenderías a leer en pocos meses.
gerund = *si estudiaras*: if you studied every night

items.spanish: De no haber existido la campaña, muchas personas no habrían aprendido a leer.
items.english: Had the campaign not existed, many people would not have learned to read.

items.spanish: De ser necesario, los brigadistas se quedaban a dormir en la casa de la familia.
items.english: If necessary, the volunteer teachers stayed to sleep in the family's house.

items.spanish: De haber sabido leer, muchos campesinos habrían podido escribir cartas.
items.english: Had they known how to read, many peasants could have written letters.

items.spanish: Estudiando cada noche, aprenderías a leer en pocos meses.
items.english: If you studied every night, you would learn to read in a few months.

sections.content: After *de* the verb is always an infinitive: *De haberlo sabido*, never *De hubiera sabido*. The main clause shows the time: conditional perfect (*habrían aprendido*) for the past, present or imperfect for a real condition. A gerund condition shares its subject with the main clause.
